structural-causal.name: bottleneckControl
structural-causal.basis: Embedded workflows, CMDB/context, governance and cross-system action create coordination value and switching friction.

structural-causal.name: crossDivisionLeverage
structural-causal.basis: IT, security/risk, CRM and employee workflows share platform context and action infrastructure.

structural-causal.name: substitutionResilience
structural-causal.basis: Deep workflow integration is sticky, but hyperscalers, application suites and model vendors can expand orchestration/governance capabilities.

structural-causal.name: scenarioRobustness
structural-causal.basis: A model-agnostic control layer can remain useful across changing AI models if customers continue to value governed cross-system workflows.

adversarial-red-team.name: financialOperatingMomentum

adversarial-red-team.name: scenarioRobustness
adversarial-red-team.basis: Platform breadth supports resilience, but competitive and technology change can shift orchestration value toward hyperscalers, model vendors or application suites.

items.risk: AI ACV and deployment growth do not alone prove durable incremental margins or defensibility against platform competitors.
Q2 included some U.S. Federal on-premise revenue accelerated from Q3, so quarterly cadence should not be extrapolated mechanically.
Control-layer value depends on measurable workflow outcomes and interoperability, not deployment counts or AI branding alone.
Quarterly revenue cadence benefited from federal on-premise timing acceleration and should not be extrapolated mechanically.
AI control/orchestration faces competitive response from hyperscalers, application suites and model vendors.
Longer customer commitments increase visibility but RPO is not equivalent to realized margin or cash flow.
Rapid AI product expansion raises execution, security, privacy and integration complexity.
